name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,354

clue.text: Opposed announcement of defensive structure

indicators.note: an announcement is spoken out, so the word for the structure is heard rather than read

blocks.note: a fort is a fortified military building

explanation.surface: Someone objects to a public notice about a new military fortification.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent FORT and FOUGHT sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: To have fought a proposal is to have resisted or campaigned against it, the past tense of opposing.

clue.text: Body to blend short beer

indicators.note: something short has been cut, so the drink loses its final letter

blocks.note: to fuse is to melt together or combine
a light bottom-fermented beer

explanation.surface: A brewing instruction about mixing a body of liquid with a weak beer.
explanation.walkthrough: LAGER loses its R to leave LAGE, and FUSE + LAGE gives FUSELAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: The fuselage is the main central structure of an aircraft, its body to which wings and tail attach.

clue.text: One reportedly supported form of investment

indicators.note: reportedly means as people say it, so the word for supported is taken by its sound

blocks.note: a unit is a single thing, one
trussed means held up by a framework of beams

explanation.surface: A claim that one person was said to back a particular way of putting money to work.
explanation.walkthrough: TRUSSED and TRUST sound almost identical said quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit trust is a pooled fund where investors buy units, a common British savings product.

clue.text: Look for something new in shed

indicators.note: in places the new thing inside the hut-like building

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for new
a hut is a small simple shed

explanation.surface: Searching for a fresh item stored in the garden shed.
explanation.walkthrough: N goes inside HUT to give HUNT.
explanation.definitionFit: To hunt for something is to search diligently, a direct synonym of looking for it.

clue.text: Steel casing

blocks.note: surface reading: a housing or shell made of steel metal
cryptic reading: steel stands for a sword, and this is the sheath that holds one

explanation.walkthrough: Steel is poetic shorthand for a blade, so the casing is not made of steel but holds it.
explanation.definitionFit: A scabbard is the sheath worn at the belt to hold a sword or dagger blade.

clue.text: Right to replace students in university procession

indicators.note: to replace means one item is swapped in where another stood

blocks.note: a college is a university institution
two learners, each L as on a learner driver's plate
RT is the standard abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A rule that changes which students take part in a university parade.
explanation.walkthrough: In COLLEGE the LL is swapped for RT, giving CO-RT-EGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A cortege is a solemn line of mourners or vehicles, especially at a funeral, so a kind of procession.

clue.text: He's aborted newly formed paper

indicators.note: something newly formed has been made over, so these letters take a fresh order

blocks.note: the letters of these words, used as written

explanation.surface: A man has abandoned a newspaper he had only just started up.
explanation.definitionFit: A broadsheet is a large-format newspaper, traditionally the more serious kind of paper.

clue.text: Stenographer holds back gas

indicators.note: the word holds the letters inside itself, so they are found within it
back means the letters are read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: the run of letters in the middle of the word

explanation.surface: A shorthand typist keeps a gas from escaping.
explanation.walkthrough: sten(OGRA)pher with the N: reading NOGRA from right to left gives ARGON.
explanation.definitionFit: Argon is an inert noble gas that makes up about one percent of air.

clue.text: After getting fresh start disappear with European

indicators.note: a fresh start means the opening letter is exchanged for a different one

blocks.note: to vanish is to disappear

explanation.surface: Someone vanishes alongside a European after starting afresh somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: VANISH gets a new first letter, D, to make DANISH; the clue leaves the replacement letter for the definition to settle.
explanation.definitionFit: Danish means from Denmark, and a Dane is a northern European.

clue.text: Outwardly struck by score's outline

indicators.note: outwardly points to the outside of the word, its first and last letters only

blocks.note: the two end letters of the word
to score a surface is to cut lines into it, to etch it

explanation.surface: A musician is moved by the shape of a musical score.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A sketch is a rough drawing or brief description giving the general outline of something.

clue.text: Small folded napkin put before the Queen.  It is used before the main course

definitions.text: It is used before the main course

indicators.note: folding a cloth rearranges it, so the letters are turned into a new order

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small
the letters of the table linen, rearranged
Elizabeth Regina, the Queen's cipher

explanation.surface: A dinner-table scene: a little folded napkin set before the Queen ahead of the main course.
explanation.walkthrough: The main course is not food but the mainsail; this large sail is set forward of it when running before the wind.
explanation.definitionFit: A spinnaker is a big balloon-shaped headsail flown at the front of a yacht, ahead of the main course or mainsail.

clue.text: Men improve after removing one part of the body

indicators.note: removing one means a single letter I, the Roman one, is taken out

blocks.note: other ranks, ordinary soldiers as opposed to officers
to gain is to make progress or get better

explanation.surface: Men get better once surgeons take out a body part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Men' here is the military sense, ordinary soldiers, and 'one' is the Roman numeral removed.
explanation.definitionFit: An organ such as the heart or liver is a distinct functional part of the body.

clue.text: Musical instrument left by pickup truck

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for left
ute is Australian slang for a utility vehicle, a pickup

explanation.surface: A guitar-like instrument abandoned beside a pickup truck.
explanation.definitionFit: The lute is a plucked string instrument with a pear-shaped body, popular in Renaissance music.

clue.text: Key workers limit time to look after servants

indicators.note: to limit is to bound on both sides, so these outer pieces surround what follows

blocks.note: A is a musical key
T is the abbreviation for time
to tend is to care for
worker ants, the classic crossword workers

explanation.surface: Essential staff put a cap on hours spent caring for domestic help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key workers' reads as one phrase for essential staff, but it splits into a musical key and insect workers, which then wrap round the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Attendants are people who wait on or serve others, so servants in a general sense.

clue.text: Reasonable game includes golf attraction?

indicators.note: includes means the pair of words takes in an extra letter between them

blocks.note: fair means just and reasonable
G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a round is one game, as of golf

explanation.surface: A fair round of golf as the draw of a day out.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the definition is an example: a fairground is one sort of attraction.
explanation.definitionFit: A fairground with its rides and stalls draws visitors, so it is a kind of entertainment attraction.

clue.text: Tear a strip off half a piece of breaded chicken before making stew

indicators.note: half means only the first three of the six letters are kept

blocks.note: a goujon is a strip of fish or chicken coated in breadcrumbs and fried
to tear a strip off someone is to scold them, to lash them verbally

explanation.surface: A cook rips up breaded chicken pieces before turning them into a stew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tear a strip off' looks like a cooking instruction but is British slang for giving someone a scolding.
explanation.definitionFit: Goulash is a Hungarian meat and paprika stew.

clue.text: Evocative memories of city gardens

blocks.note: EC is the postcode of the City of London
to hoe is to work the soil in a garden

explanation.surface: Someone nostalgically recalling the parks of a city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gardens' is a verb here, not the parks the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: Echoes are traces or reminders of the past that call earlier times back to mind.

clue.text: Hold the attention of adult through internet broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast suggests scattering seed widely, so the letters are strewn into a new order

blocks.note: A is the film classification for adult
used as written

explanation.surface: Keeping a grown-up audience engaged by streaming online.
explanation.definitionFit: To entertain someone is to amuse them and keep them interested, holding their attention.

clue.text: Learned old money is held by European editor

indicators.note: held by means gripped on both sides by the following letters

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for European
a ducat was a gold coin once used across Europe
ED is the standard short form of editor

explanation.surface: A scholar's old coin collection is in the keeping of a European newspaper editor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Learned' is the two-syllable adjective, not the past tense of learn.
explanation.definitionFit: Learned means scholarly and well-taught, having had a thorough schooling.

clue.text: Deny rebel leader is in bar

indicators.note: the leader is the one at the front, so only the opening letter is used
in places that letter inside the word for a bar

blocks.note: the initial letter of the word
a stave is a wooden bar or rod

explanation.surface: Turning away a rebel chief who is drinking in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' suggests a pub, but here it is a rod of wood.
explanation.definitionFit: To starve someone of something is to withhold it from them, to deprive or refuse them it.

clue.text: Leading movement written up in publication

indicators.note: in a down entry, written up means the letters run from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: number one, NO 1, is the leader
the tide is the regular movement of the sea

explanation.surface: A leading artistic movement gets a write-up in a magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: NO I (number one) + TIDE is NOITIDE, read upwards as EDITION.
explanation.definitionFit: An edition is one issue or version of a published book, newspaper or magazine.

clue.text: Gathered onset of death follows dish laced with drug

indicators.note: a dish laced with something has it mixed into it, so a letter goes inside
the onset is the beginning, so only the first letter is taken

blocks.note: a plate is a dish
E is ecstasy
first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A poisoning mystery: death comes soon after a meal spiked with a drug.
explanation.walkthrough: E goes into PLATE, giving PLEATE, and D follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Fabric that is gathered is drawn into folds, as pleated cloth is.

clue.text: Metal seat at Metro is oddly missing

indicators.note: with the odd-placed letters missing, only the even ones survive

blocks.note: a pew is a bench seat in a church
the second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: A commuter notices that the metal seat at the Metro station has strangely gone.
explanation.definitionFit: Pewter is a grey alloy mostly of tin, a metal used for tankards and plates.

clue.text: A person of little value produces secret code

blocks.note: first meaning: a nobody, someone of no importance
second meaning: a system of encrypted writing

explanation.surface: An unimportant underling turns out to have written a coded message.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a zero or nonentity and a method of encrypting a message.

clue.text: Trainee doctor briefly has to contend with Pole's questions

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the last letter is dropped

blocks.note: an intern is a junior hospital doctor in training
to vie is to compete
W is the abbreviation for with
S is the south pole

explanation.surface: A junior doctor must face a Polish patient's questions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' looks like a nationality, but it is a magnetic pole, S; the 's adds it after W.
explanation.definitionFit: To interview someone is to question them formally, so as a verb it means questions.

clue.text: Works with Mr Lowry to support you in France

blocks.note: toi is the familiar French for you
L S Lowry, the English painter of industrial scenes

explanation.surface: Paintings by Lowry being sent to back up a French friend.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, a piece that supports another sits beneath it. Lowry is the painter of matchstick figures in northern mill towns.
explanation.definitionFit: Toils as a verb means labours hard and at length.

clue.text: Animal regularly seen in car porch

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is picked out

blocks.note: the first, third, fifth and seventh letters

explanation.surface: A pet often spotted lurking in a carport.
explanation.walkthrough: C-a-R-p-O-r-C-h: the odd letters spell the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A croc, short for crocodile, is a large reptile, an animal.

clue.text: Star comes back in luggage-van

indicators.note: coming back means travelling the opposite way, so the letters are read backwards
in means the letters lie inside the following words

blocks.note: the run of letters across the hyphen

explanation.surface: A celebrity returns home riding in the baggage car.
explanation.walkthrough: lugg(AGE-V)an read backwards gives VEGA.
explanation.definitionFit: Vega is the brightest star in the constellation Lyra, one of the brightest in the sky.

clue.text: Human rights group in Chinese territory texted you in verse

indicators.note: in places the group's letters within the territory's abbreviation

blocks.note: Hong Kong
Amnesty International
in text-speak you is written as the single letter

explanation.surface: A campaign group in Hong Kong sends a poem by text message.
explanation.walkthrough: Text-speak shortens 'you' to its sound, a single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A haiku is a short Japanese poem of seventeen syllables, a form of verse.

clue.text: Clumsy fellow leaves position with soldier

indicators.note: leaves means goes away from, so a letter departs

blocks.note: F is the abbreviation for fellow
fine leg is a fielding position in cricket, behind the batsman on the leg side
a soldier ant

explanation.surface: An awkward man quits his post alongside a serviceman.
explanation.walkthrough: FINE LEG loses its F to give INELEG, then ANT. Fine leg is a cricket position.
explanation.definitionFit: Inelegant means lacking grace or polish, so awkward or clumsy in manner or movement.

clue.text: Let team in for householder

indicators.note: in places the side inside the word for letting

blocks.note: to let a property is to rent it out
a side is a sports team

explanation.surface: A landlord lets a sports team move in, in place of the homeowner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Let' looks like 'allow' but is the property sense, to lease out.
explanation.definitionFit: A resident is someone who lives in a house, an occupier or householder.

clue.text: Prohibited Australian outlaw tailed by group briefly

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the last letter is dropped

blocks.note: a band is a group
Ned Kelly, the famous Australian bushranger

explanation.surface: An outlaw from Australia is shadowed by a gang.
explanation.walkthrough: BAND shortened to BAN is joined by NED; the outlaw is read as the tail on the shortened group.
explanation.definitionFit: Banned means forbidden by rule or law, the same as prohibited.
